name: The Hope Conspiracy
label: Deathwish
lede: Boston hardcore with a snarl and a reading list. Four albums in twenty-five years, most of them cut at Kurt Ballou's Godcity, and Kevin Baker is still angry on the newest one.

eras.title: A demo from Norwood
eras.text: Bassist Jonas Feinberg and singer Kevin Baker start the band in late 1999. A three-song demo and a room at Kurt Ballou's Godcity get them onto Equal Vision within a year.

years.h: The Hope Conspiracy press 1,000 demo cassettes
years.p: The band record three songs in Norwood, Massachusetts: "Escapist," "Divinity Sickness" and "When the Doves Fly," later retitled "Regret Kills."
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the band pressed 1,000 cassette copies. The demo later came out on CD and 7-inch through Aaron Turner's involvement, and Wikipedia lists it as a self-titled demo on Life Recordings with a fourth track added later.

Baker's earlier band was Piecemeal, per a 2024 interview on The New Scene podcast.

years.p: Bassist [[Jonas Feinberg|9ce65b6a-2494-4214-8180-765f33a5586c]] and singer [[Kevin Baker|f9206d8b-3a1d-4336-be61-7b656aa1b6e8]] start the band in Boston with guitarist Neeraj Kane, Dan Zimmerman on guitar and Adam Patterson on drums.
years.xp: Grokipedia credits Feinberg with forming the band in late 1999. His earlier band, per the same page, was Harvest, which is the weaker of the two sources on this.

years.h: Cold Blue arrives on Equal Vision, 22 minutes long
years.p: Ten songs, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] producing. Equal Vision Records puts it out on October 24, 2000.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it was recorded at Godcity Studios and The Outpost in Stoughton, Massachusetts.

Exclaim! liked the approach, saying Baker's lyrics were "more poetic than preaching" next to most hardcore of the day.

eras.title: Endnote, and a revolving guitar slot
eras.text: Bridge 9 and Equal Vision each get a record, guitarist Aaron Lisi and drummer Jarrod Alexander pass through, and by 2003 the band goes quiet.

years.h: File 03 slips out on Bridge 9 between two albums
years.p: Bridge 9 Records issues the short release between the two Equal Vision records.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as a reissue of the demo tracks plus two new songs.

years.p: Equal Vision releases the second album in autumn 2002, and Punknews gives it 4.5 out of 5.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it was recorded in May and June 2002 at Atomic Studios in Brooklyn and produced by Dean Baltunosis, so Ballou is not on this one. It lists the release as October 17, 2002 on the band page and September 17 on the album page, so the file says 2002 only.

Drummer [[Jarrod Alexander|175a4ea4-8b0c-4d9b-b09e-625372f6ff44]], also of [[Suicide File|86336490-e9fb-41e3-9a81-8edfa56785ec]], plays on the record. He later joined [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]] live in 2011.

years.h: A split 7-inch with Suicide File lands on Deathwish
years.p: The band share the record with Suicide File on [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s Deathwish Inc.. Wikipedia lists "Failure" as the Hope Conspiracy track.

years.h: Jim Carroll replaces Aaron Lisi and moves into the practice space
years.p: Jim Carroll joins in about August 2003 and lives at 12 Wadsworth, the practice space where Feinberg also lives.
years.xp: Baker told Scene Point Blank why: "I especially like The Suicide File so it was a no brainer."

eras.title: Death Knows Your Name
eras.text: Back with a fresh lineup and a new label, the band make the record fans still name first, then one more EP and a quiet exit.

years.h: Baker joins Bars while the band sits idle
years.p: [[Jared Shavelson|b0eea190-59fa-402a-8883-4135d11a1d13]] drums for [[None More Black|a1f28c75-e6aa-4d63-9b01-3be42c599fab]] in the meantime.
years.xp: Baker has described personal struggles during the break in an interview. Grokipedia adds that Feinberg worked as a live sound engineer for Bleeding Through.

years.h: A year at Godcity, then Death Knows Your Name
years.p: Recorded February 2005 to February 2006 with Kurt Ballou, it comes out on Deathwish on September 19, 2006.
years.xp:
Baker said they wanted it raw, with reference copies of Entombed's Uprising and Zeke's Till the Living End lying around the console.

[[Dwid Hellion|1f27f407-dbbb-4d9a-b186-fdf5a613a855]] of [[Integrity|f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a]] recorded vocals for "Sadistic Sacred Whore" alone in Belgium. "We spoke via AIM and I just sent him a copy of the song," Baker said, and Hellion sent the files to Ballou at Godcity.

Neeraj Kane returned and Tim Cossar joined for the record.

years.h: The Hang Your Cross EP leaves "Eurohell" for the reissue
years.p: A short EP from the same stretch as the album. "Eurohell" turns up as the bonus track on the 2022 reissue.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it on Deathwish as vinyl, with Resist Records handling the CD.

years.h: True Nihilist is the last record for fifteen years
years.p: Deathwish puts out the 7-inch, again recorded by Ballou at Godcity.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Ballou with recording it at Godcity.

eras.title: Baker's other band, and a long wait
eras.text: Baker moves to All Pigs Must Die. The old band spends a decade apart before committing to each other again.

years.h: Baker moves to All Pigs Must Die with Converge's Ben Koller
years.p: The band forms in 2009 around [[Ben Koller|b6fdd346-b9e8-449a-9105-612d3722503f]], and Baker keeps the mic through 2017.

years.cap: Kevin Baker and the band, Los Angeles, Sept 2024
years.h: "We aren't getting any younger," Baker says, and the band writes again
years.p: The Hope Conspiracy commit to new songs in spring 2022.
years.xp:
They recorded music in fall 2022 at Godcity, and Baker later did his vocals in a home studio.

In the New Noise interview he said the album had been done for about a year, so having it come out was "a relief since we are not getting any younger."

years.h: Deathwish reissues Death Knows Your Name with a bonus track
years.p: Wikipedia dates the remastered reissue to 2022, and it adds "Eurohell".

eras.title: Tools of Oppression
eras.text: A new EP and a new album, both cut at Godcity, and the first stages in years.

years.cap: The Hope Conspiracy at 1720, Los Angeles, Sept 6, 2024
years.p: Ballou and Zach Weeks engineer the new EP, the first fresh material in about fifteen years.
years.xp: Grokipedia dates the announcement to November 22, 2023 and says the EP came out on Deathwish vinyl.

years.h: Tools of Oppression/Rule by Deception is the fourth album
years.p: Deathwish releases it in May 2024, recorded at Godcity with Ballou and Weeks.
years.xp:
Baker told New Noise it was the first time he could remember feeling that way about a record he'd worked on. "Kurt and Zach were very open to our ideas," he said.

The album takes aim at oligarchy. "The greatest lie people keep believing is that we live in a democracy," Baker said. "This is an oligarchy." For the song "Of a Dying Nation" he listed "fear, loathing, mezcal, mushrooms and Killing Joke."

years.cap: Baker on stage, Los Angeles, Sept 6, 2024
years.h: The first shows in nearly fifteen years
years.p: They tour North America and, per Grokipedia, Europe in 2025.
years.xp: Grokipedia dates the first live show to June 8, 2024 and lists 2025 dates in Detroit, Denver, Mexico City and Boston.
